title: feat(spec): `IJobService.replay` gains an optional `options?: JobReplayOptions` argument carrying `force: true` (#14766)
body:
Fixes #14766

The contract half of the maintainer's A + a2 ruling on #14501 (#14501 remains open — its behaviour half lands there, and it is what this card unblocks). `IJobService.replay` in `packages/spec/src/contracts/job-service.ts` gains an optional third argument:

```ts
replay?(name: string, data?: unknown, options?: JobReplayOptions)   // still a Promise resolving to void
```

## Shape: an options object, not a positional boolean

`JobReplayOptions { force?: boolean }` is exported from `@objectstack/spec` (the `contracts` entry). Chosen over a bare positional `force?: boolean` because this interface already follows the named-options convention for the same kind of knob — `schedule(name, schedule, handler, options?: JobScheduleOptions)` — and no spec-wide convention prefers a positional boolean: every other optional trailing argument across `packages/spec/src/contracts/*.ts` is an options object (`analytics-service`, `automation-service`, `data-driver.beginTransaction`, `metadata-service.publishPackage` / `rollback` / `bulkRegister`, `package-service.listPackages`, `queue-service`). `replay(name, data, { force: true })` says what it does at the call site; a later knob is a second key on the interface, never a fourth positional. Omitting the argument is the pre-#14766 call exactly.

## What the TSDoc declares — the text the #14501 implementer codes against

For a scheduled (cron) flow whose tick window takes a `(flow, tick-window)` dispatch claim in `sys_flow_dispatch`:

- claim **absent** or **failed** — `replay(name, data)` re-runs the window (unchanged behaviour); every job that never takes a claim is this row;
- claim **succeeded** — `replay(name, data)` is **refused loudly**: the promise rejects with an ADR-0112 envelope, `code: 'RESOURCE_CONFLICT'` (the standard-catalog member HTTP 409 derives — `HttpStatusErrorCodeMap[409]` in `api/errors.zod.ts`) and `status: 409`, whose message names the window asked for and the claim that refused it. Never a silent no-op, never a resolve-having-done-nothing;
- `replay(name, data, { force: true })` sends anyway (option a2). Options a1 and a3 are recorded in the doc block as considered and not taken.

Why the standard-catalog member rather than a new extension code: registering a `JOB_*` code in `error-code-ledger.zod.ts` before any producer exists is the declared-but-unproduced shape ADR-0112's 2026-08-18 amendment retired from the catalog; the 409 member is closed vocabulary already, and a consumer asserts the refusal on `code` + `status`. Should #14501 find a console needs to branch on this refusal distinctly from other 409s, an extension code is that card's to register together with its producer (raised as an open question in the dev report).

## In this PR

- the declaration + TSDoc, and the exported `JobReplayOptions` interface
- `job-service.test.ts`: a compile-time pin block — a two-argument implementation stays assignable (additivity); `{ force: true }` is accepted through the exported type; the third parameter is identical to `JobReplayOptions | undefined` (identity, not assignability); `force` is the only member and a boolean — plus a source-reading pin that the doc block names the three claim states, the ADR-0112 envelope with `code` and `status`, the window, the claim and the `force` door
- regenerated `api-surface/contracts.json` and `export-origins/contracts.json` — exactly the two artifacts `check:generated --fix` proved stale; `src/migrations/registry.ts` and `authorable-surface.base.json` are untouched
- changeset `.changeset/job-service-replay-force.md`, `@objectstack/spec` minor, stating that the refusal semantics are declared here and enforced by #14501
- no liveness-ledger row names `replay`: `liveness/job.json` governs `JobSchema` properties, and contract methods are not ledger rows — nothing to add
- no ADR-0087 entry: additive optional parameter, nothing retired; `check:migration-registry` and `check:adr-0087-registration --self-test` are green

## Out of scope, verified untouched

`DbJobAdapter.replay` (`packages/services/service-job/src/db-job-adapter.ts`) keeps compiling with no edit: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-job typecheck` against the rebuilt spec dist — `os-verify-lock: VERDICT command-exit 0`. No behaviour, no `sys_flow_dispatch`, no `schedule-trigger.ts`, no pin outside `packages/spec`.
